comparisons.peer_topic: Responsible Business Alliance Membership and Ethical Standards
comparisons.peer_summary: As a member of the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA), the company strives to adhere to its Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and the RBA code of conduct to promote responsible working conditions and ethical business practices in its global supply chain.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron explicitly reference the Responsible Business Alliance (RBA) as a framework for supplier compliance and ethical standards. Intel describes engaging with suppliers to verify compliance with the RBA and Intel Code of Conduct through audits and capability-building programs (S001, S002), while Micron states its membership in the RBA and adherence to its code of conduct to promote responsible practices (S001, S002). Both disclosures link RBA membership to broader supply chain ethics.

sentences.text: We perform periodic audits and identify critical direct suppliers to engage through capability-building programs, which help suppliers build sustainability acumen and verify compliance with the Responsible Business Alliance and the Intel Code of Conduct.

We are a member of the Responsible Business Alliance ("RBA"), a group of leading companies focused on promoting responsible working conditions, ethical business practices, and environmental stewardship throughout our global supply chain.

We strive to adhere to both our Code of Business Conduct and Ethics (available on our website, www.micron.com) and the RBA code of conduct, which is a demonstration of our commitment to integrity and responsible practices.

comparisons.peer_summary: By fiscal year 2026, NVIDIA aims to engage manufacturing suppliers comprising at least 67% of its scope 3 category 1 GHG emissions to adopt science-based targets.
comparisons.comparison: While Intel focuses on auditing for human rights and code of conduct compliance, NVIDIA focuses on engaging suppliers for environmental emissions reduction targets. Intel engages suppliers to verify compliance with the Responsible Business Alliance and Intel Code of Conduct (S002), whereas NVIDIA aims to engage manufacturing suppliers to adopt science-based targets for Scope 3 GHG emissions (S006). Both represent supplier engagement initiatives within the supply chain, but Intel's focus is ethical compliance audits while NVIDIA's is environmental performance.

comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm's 2025 goals include reducing absolute Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions by 30% from a 2014 base year, reducing power consumption in flagship Snapdragon Mobile Platform products by 10% annually, and ensuring 100% of primary semiconductor manufacturing suppliers are audited every two years for conformance to the Supplier Code of Conduct.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Qualcomm disclose formal supplier audit programs related to corporate responsibility and code of conduct compliance. Intel reports performing periodic audits on direct suppliers to verify compliance with the RBA and Intel Code of Conduct (S002). Qualcomm lists a 2025 goal where 100% of primary semiconductor manufacturing suppliers are audited every two years for conformance to its Supplier Code of Conduct (S005). Both firms use audits as a mechanism for supply chain verification.
